newsitem.title: UK: Royal Bank of Scotland full year profits up.
newsitem.headline: Royal Bank of Scotland full year profits up.

text.p: Royal Bank of Scotland said Thursday its full-year pretax profits rose by 15 percent 695.0 million pounds ($1.17 billion), as strong growth in its British and U.S. banking operations offset a dip at its insurance unit.

Royal Bank said its U.S. bank Citizens, based in New England, lifted profits by 61 million pounds ($102.4 million), or 57 percent, adding that it will continue its strategy of deepening its franchise and expanding its core business.
Profits were also higher in UK Banking, rising 97 million pounds ($162.9 million) or 22 percent.

However, Direct Line, which sells motor, house and life insurance, saw profits shrink by 86 million pounds ($144.4 million) to 26 million ($43.7 million) for the year as premium rates remained pressure and claims increased.

The Royal Bank figures included a 72 million pound ($120.9 million) gain from the sale of an interest in a German bank and a cost of 21 million pounds ($35.3 million) from restructuring an acquisition by Citizens.
